subject: Design options for auth, SDK bootstrapping, and embeddings pipeline — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design options for auth, SDK bootstrapping, and embeddings pipeline — follow-up

Hi Sam — great chat today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned: 

1) Goals we heard
- Pilot: low-risk sandbox to validate embeddings + reranker for search relevance on transactions data
- Production: ~500 qps embeddings lookup, latency SLO 200ms for search path, budget-conscious (target infra cost < $X/token)

2) Auth & key management constraints you flagged
- Need auditable key rotation and short-lived credentials for production
- Prefer service accounts for backend-to-backend calls; security team asked about OAuth/JWT for user-scoped flows
- Procurement needs a simple integration path to avoid long legal delays

3) Integration surface we discussed
- SDK bootstrapping (Python + Node) with built-in retry/backoff and routing hooks (region & cost tier)
- Structured output/tool-calling for enrichment (we demoed a prototype of function-calling for entity normalization)
- Embeddings -> reranker pipeline: option to host reranker with Redwood or run locally with Redwood embeddings API

4) Proposed immediate next steps
- I will share a short tech proposal (auth options + recommended default) for your security team by Monday. [attached: redwood-auth-options.pdf]
- We can spin up a sandbox instance (hosted) for POC within 5 business days after PO; I put an SDK mini-playbook in the attachment for quick start. [attached: sdk-bootstrapping-playbook.md]
- Rishi (cc'd) will follow up on the token rotation diagram and specific service-account patterns we recommend for your infra.

Questions for you (one-line answers appreciated):
- Who on your side will own the security questionnaire? (security@?)
- Do you want us to default the pilot to API keys in sandbox or start with short-lived JWTs?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the attachments and a one-page tech summary for Security.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-auth-options.pdf, sdk-bootstrapping-playbook.md

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from my side after looping in Security and Procurement: 

- Security: we prefer short-lived JWTs for any user-scoped requests and service accounts with rotating keys for server-to-server. They want to see a concrete rotation cadence (e.g., 24h or 7d) and HSM/KMS compatibility.
- Procurement: request for an initial SOC2 artifact and a sample contract appendix for data handling.
- POC preference: start with API keys in sandbox to get data in quickly, but must have a clear migration path to JWT/service-account before production.

Can you have the tech summary focus on: rotation cadence options, how Redwood routes requests between hosted/dedicated/private (we care about the routing decisions for cost vs latency), and a sample SDK flow that shows embedding calls -> reranker service?

If you can get that to security@ and procure@ by Monday that would help keep timeline tight.

—Sam

Sam — following up with the tech proposal attached and our recommended defaults. High level summary + ask for Security and Procurement below. Attachments included: redwood-auth-options.pdf (detailed tradeoffs), sdk-bootstrapping-playbook.md (copy/paste scripts), token-rotation-diagram.png

Key recommendation (short):
- Sandbox: API keys with expiration + usage quotas (fastest onboarding)
- Production: service accounts (JWTs) issued by your KMS; Redwood supports OIDC + JWT verification and can accept short-lived signed tokens for server-to-server auth. We recommend 24h rotation for SA tokens with automated rotation via your KMS/HSM.
- For user-scoped flows (if you expose user-level write ops) use OAuth2 with consent; otherwise keep user requests proxied by backend using service accounts.
- Routing: default routing policy is region-first -> cost-tier fallback. For your production SLOs, we recommend dedicated capacity for the hot reranker and hosted embeddings for scale.

ATTN Security: please see pages 3–5 in redwood-auth-options.pdf for rotation mechanics and KMS integrations. We included an explicit example for Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS.

ATTN Procurement: sample appendix is on the final page of the pdf; we can extract it and add to your PO.

Action items I propose now:
- Security: confirm acceptable rotation cadence window (24h vs 7d) and KMS vendor (AWS/Azure/GCP) by Tue 31 May
- Procurement: share preferred PO template or confirm digital signature process by Tue 31 May
- Engineering (Rishi): please review token-rotation-diagram.png and add any Redwood-specific implementation notes (service account bootstrap commands, short-lived JWT example) — want to share the final doc to Security by Monday EOD.

Forwarded message below for full context.

Thanks Marissa — reviewed the diagram and the PDF. A few concrete engineering notes for the plan we recommend shipping to Security/Procurement: 

1) Service-account bootstrap (recommended)- Provide a short script that creates a signed JWT with a 24h exp claim, stored in your KMS; Redwood accepts OIDC-signed assertions or direct JWTs for server-to-server auth. Example flow in sdk-bootstrapping-playbook.md lines 42–58.

2) Rotation cadence- 24h rotation is safest for production; we can support 7d for lower-risk non-prod with audit logs. Rotation is automated via KMS API and we emit rotation events to your audit log (we can push via webhook to your SIEM).

3) Key compromise mitigation- We recommend two-tier keys: short-lived SA tokens for day-to-day, and a signing key in HSM for token issuance. If a token is suspected compromised, revoke via KMS and rotate signing key; Redwood supports immediate cache invalidation for tokens.

4) Embeddings/reranker routing- For your target latency, place the reranker on Dedicated; embeddings throughput is cheaper and can run hosted with region affinity. SDK will include a routing hook: prefer dedicated-reranker endpoint for search requests, fallback to hosted-reranker for bursts.

I added a short snippet to the playbook describing an HTTP header we use for routing: X-Redwood-Route: zone=us-east1;tier=dedicated. 

If that aligns, I’ll add a one-page appendix to redwood-auth-options.pdf describing the exact API calls for rotate/revoke and a curl example for short-lived JWT exchange.

—Rishi
